newsitem.title: UK: Gehe posts Lloyds Chemist offer.
newsitem.headline: Gehe posts Lloyds Chemist offer.

text.p: Germany pharmaceutical company Gehe AG said on Monday it had posted its offer document in a long-running battle to buy Britain's Lloyd's Chemists Plc.

Gehe, Europe's largest drug distributor which last month launched a fresh 650.6 million pound bid for Lloyds, said its offer document, which sets the 60-day bid timetable ticking, would be open initially until December 23.

A verbal war between Gehe and its British bidding rival for Lloyds, UniChem Plc, has raged since both companies first launched takeover bids earlier this year. But both bids lapsed in March after being referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
The new bid by Unichem, which already owns 9.9 percent of Lloyds, values the UK drugs group at 657.6 million pounds in a cash and paper bid.
Gehe, which is offering an all cash bid at 500p for each Lloyds share and 322.6p for each preference share, insisted that its bid was "highly attractive."
"By making a largely share offer, UniChem is exposing Lloyds Chemists' shareholders to an uncertain future earnings stream and uncertain value," Dieter Kammerer, Gehe's chairman, said in a statement.
"Lloyd's Chemists' shareholders can avoid the risks involved in taking UniChem shares by accepting Gehe's cash offers," he added.
